'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
***[[War in Donbas]]
****The [[Ukrainian government]] accuses [[Russian separatist forces in Donbas|Russian separatists]] of shelling a [[kindergarten]] in [[Stanytsia Luhanska]], [[Luhansk Oblast]] using [[artillery]], injuring three civilians. The [[Luhansk People's Republic]] says that its forces were attacked by the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian military]] with [[mortar (weapon)|mortars]], [[grenade launcher]]s and [[machine gun]] fire. At least 32 shells hit the city, causing power outages and damaging multiple structures. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/west-accuses-russia-of-trying-to-create-pretext-for-invasion-after-shelling-in-east-ukraine/ar-AATZcQu?ocid=uxbndlbing (MSN)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/feb/17/shelling-by-russian-backed-separatists-hits-school-in-east-ukraine (''The Guardian'')]
****The [[United Nations Security Council]] convenes in order to discuss [[Russia]]'s [[Russian Armed Forces|military]] buildup on the [[Russia-Ukraine border|Ukrainian border]]. [https://www.c-span.org/video/?518019-1/secretary-blinken-russia-preparing-manufacture-pretext-invading-ukraine (C-SPAN)]
****The U.S. State Department confirms that the U.S. deputy ambassador to Russia was expelled from the country. [[White House Office of the Press Secretary|White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary]] [[Karine Jean-Pierre]] calls the expulsion "unprovoked". [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/russia-expulsion-of-us-deputy-ambassador-unprovoked-white-house/ar-AATZWWg?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters)]
****The EU [[High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy|High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy]] [[Josep Borrell]] says that [[Shell (projectile)|shelling]] has begun in [[eastern Ukraine]]. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/internacional/20220217/8064868/borrell-afirma-empezado-bombardeo-ucrania.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
***[[Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
****Senior [[government of the United Kingdom|British]] officials say that [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] has now decided to invade [[Ukraine]] following "changes in the last 24 hours". [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/satellite-reveals-russians-arriving-near-ukraine-border-npmvnbs9q (''The Times'')]
****[[Germany]] deploys 130 [[German Army|troops]] and 60 [[armoured personnel carrier]]s to [[Lithuania]]. [[Lithuanian President]] [[Gitanas Nauseda]] says that the German forces are authorized to defend the country from threats. More troops are expected to arrive later this week. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/german-army-reinforcements-reach-lithuania-amid-ukraine-crisis-2022-02-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]], [[Operation Barkhane]]
**[[France]] and the [[European Union|EU]]-wide [[Takuba Task Force]] announce that they will begin withdrawing from [[Mali]], stating that the [[government of Mali|military government]] in place since [[2021 Malian coup d'état|last year's coup]] has placed "multiple obstructions" to their [[counter-terrorism]] operations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/2/17/france-allies-announce-military-withdrawal-from-mali (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Panama]]-flagged [[Roll-on/roll-off#Car carriers|car carrier]] MV ''Felicity Ace'' is abandoned approximately 90 nautical miles southwest of [[Azores|the Azores]] following a severe fire onboard. The ship's entire 22-man crew safely evacuates using lifeboats. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/17/tech/ship-fire-luxury-cars/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[British Columbia]] lifts most of its [[COVID-19]] restrictions, allowing all businesses to reopen and operate at full capacity. Indoor gatherings and organized events are also permitted to operate without occupancy limits. However, provincial mandates requiring the use of [[COVID-19 vaccine card|vaccine cards]] for entry into businesses and the use of [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|masks]] in indoor settings remain in effect. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/covid-restrictions-update-1.6352614 (CBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] announces that [[California]] will become the first [[U.S. state]] to [[Endemic phase of COVID-19|approach]] COVID-19 as an [[Endemic (epidemiology)|endemic]] rather than a [[pandemic]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-19-california-first-state-endemic-not-pandemic/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Dominican Republic]]
****The [[Dominican Republic]] ends all COVID-19-related public health measures, including mask wearing mandates and use of vaccine passes in order to enter public places, despite not reaching 70% of its vaccination target. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2022-02-17/dominican-republic-ends-mask-mandate-all-other-covid-19-rules (''U.S. News & World Report'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] surpasses 5 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.medcom.id/english/national/aNrvXw6N-covid-19-cases-in-indonesia-surpass-5-million (Medcom.id)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports a record 269 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2022021700940/japan's-daily-covid-19-death-toll-hits-record-269.html (Nippon.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] reports a record 1,929 new community transmitted COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/covid-19-omicron-outbreak-record-1929-community-cases-aucklanders-warned-of-test-result-delays/3FDFX744H4HKRNT3KPYFMLJJBE/ (''New Zealand Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
***[[President of the Swiss Confederation|Swiss President]] [[Ignazio Cassis]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2022-02-17/swiss-president-tests-positive-for-covid-19-as-country-opens (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Canada convoy protest]]
**Tamara Lich and Chris Barber, two organizers of the protest in [[Ottawa]], are arrested by police. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/canada/ottawa-police-arrest-convoy-organizers-but-others-remain-defiant-1.5785073 (CTV News)]
*[[Designated terrorist organisations in Australia]]
**[[Government of Australia|Australia]] designates the entirety of [[Hamas]], including its political wing, as a [[terrorist organisation]], and also designates [[Atomwaffen Division]], [[Tahrir al-Sham]] and the [[Guardians of Religion Organization]] as terrorist organisations. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/australia-to-list-palestinian-group-hamas-as-terrorist-organisation/a0244890-284e-49cd-844b-acdc5d44702f (SBS News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*The [[Kuwait]]i Ministers of [[Ministry of Defense (Kuwait)|Defense]] and [[Ministry of Interior (Kuwait)|the Interior]], both members of the ruling [[House of Al Sabah|Al-Sabah family]], resign. The resignations are accepted by the [[Emir of Kuwait|Emir]], who appoints a different member of the Al-Sabah family and Mohammad al-Fares, the current [[Ministry of Oil (Kuwait)|Oil Minister]], to their respective posts. [https://businesscapitalnews.com/2022/02/17/kuwaits-emir-accepts-resignations-of-defence-interior-ministers/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] ends its [[immigrant investor programs]], known as a Tier 1 (Investor) visa, with "immediate effect". The scheme was introduced in 2008 in order to encourage wealthy people from outside the [[European Union]] to invest in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-60410844 (BBC News)]
